Subject: RE: Persistent 5xx spike hitting stratus-rw-13b — initial findings & immediate mitigations

Emma / Jonas — quick update from SRE after initial triage. We pulled traces correlated to your samples and confirmed elevated 5xxs originating from the inference runtime for the "stratus-rw-13b" *quantized* execution path. Key findings so far: 

- Symptom: sudden increase in internal runtime exceptions producing 5xx responses and upstream gateway timeouts (client timeouts observed at ~10–12s).
- Trigger window: ~08:42–09:10 PT (matches your report).
- Root cause (hypothesis): a recent attention-kernel optimization in the quantized execution path regresses under high concurrent KV cache churn. Under heavy prefix sharing (common in your onboarding flows) this leads to premature KV eviction and a tensor-shape assertion in the optimized kernel.
- Why it surfaced now: higher concurrency from repeated synthetic tests + a small traffic pattern shift in Stratus demos that exercises long-prefix caching.

Immediate mitigations we've executed: 
1) Pinned Stratus traffic to the non-quantized fallback variant (rw-13b-stable) for all requests as of 10:08 PT. This reduced observed 5xxs from ~12% -> ~0.6% in your Canary session.
2) Scaled your dedicated inference pool + warm instances to reduce cold-start and network jitter (10:15 PT).
3) Disabled the problematic quantized kernel via runtime flag on affected nodes (10:22 PT).

Attached: kernel-trace-quant.log (excerpts), and we've ingested your stratus_error_log_20280118.csv into our triage tools.

Planned next steps (today):
- Controlled restart and full rollback of the kernel change across the affected pool at 02:00 UTC (recommended maintenance window) — this prevents recurring regressions.
- Run a targeted synthetic test-suite (focused on long-prefix KV caching) to validate the rollback and quant path fixes.
- Keep traffic pinned to rw-13b-stable until we validate the fix.

Timeline & commitment: we'll provide a full postmortem draft by 11:00 PT tomorrow with a list of long-term mitigations (e.g., improved kernel CI, additional canary traffic shapes, automated fallback routing).

Questions for you, Emma:
- Are you OK with the planned 02:00 UTC rollback window? (should be low-impact for your team; we'll do it in a maintenance window and confirm.)
- Do you want Redwood to run the synthetic regression suite against a copy of your traffic profile?

--
Marissa Cole
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — stratus-rw-13b 2028-01-18

Emma — thank you again for your patience while we investigated. Below is a concise post-incident summary and the concrete next steps. We will publish a fuller postmortem (internal + customer-facing) and share the doc link; attaching the draft PDF and working doc for your review.

Executive summary:
- Incident window: 2028-01-18 08:42 PT to 2028-01-18 10:22 PT (full mitigation in place at 10:22 PT).
- Impact: Elevated 5xxs (peak ~12%) and client timeouts for requests routed to the quantized execution path of stratus-rw-13b. A subset of your onboarding/demo traffic experienced degraded quality and availability during the window.
- Root cause: Regression in an attention-kernel optimization for the quantized runtime path causing premature KV cache eviction under high-concurrency long-prefix patterns. This triggered tensor-shape assertions in the optimized kernel and surfaced as internal runtime 5xxs.

Actions completed:
- Immediate: Pinned Stratus to rw-13b-stable and disabled the faulty kernel flag (10:08–10:22 PT). Scaled pool capacity for your account.
- Corrective: Performed controlled rollback in maintenance window (02:00 UTC on 2028-01-19) and ran synthetic traffic tests validating the fix.
- Compensation: Redwood will apply a goodwill invoice credit equivalent to 10% of your billed usage for Jan 2028 for the impacted window; your account team will follow up with a formal credit note.

Longer-term fixes (in flight):
- Kernel CI: Add targeted regression tests for long-prefix KV caching patterns against quantized kernels (ETA: 6 weeks).
- Canary Improvements: Introduce traffic-shape canaries that exercise long-prefix caching (ETA: 3 weeks).
- Automated Fallbacks: Implement an automated routing policy to fall back to stable variants when model-level 5xx exceeds threshold (ETA: 4 weeks).

Attachments: postmortem-stratus-20280118.pdf (customer-facing) and postmortem-draft-jonas-v1.docx (working copy).

Please reply with any questions or edits you'd like included in the customer-facing doc. We will also schedule a 30-minute postmortem review next week to walk through the timeline and proposed mitigations.

Thanks — we appreciate your partnership and will follow through on the action items.

Best,
